transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, we need to review the oral-history project draft before I can sign off on it. I'd like to go through the key elements one at a time — participation scope, supervision, data storage and retention, and the public exhibit. Let's start with the participation plan for grades 7 and 8. Does anyone have concerns or suggestions before we work through the rest?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share findings from my classroom pilot. My end-of-pilot notes show that the project is instructionally ready only for grade 8 — not grade 7. Also, each interview session requires exactly two supervising adults, not one, because students are working with recording equipment alongside community guests. The draft plan still has the original scope of grades 7 and 8 and only one supervising adult per session, so those elements need to be updated.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical privacy issue with the draft. The district privacy review, which I've already completed, requires that all recordings remain on the district's encrypted internal server — not cloud-based storage. Additionally, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the exhibit closes, not the 90-day retention period currently in the draft. Finally, signed guardian consent is required before any student records an interview. The draft still uses the preliminary cloud-storage language and the 90-day timeline, so those need to be corrected before Dr. Chen signs off.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share the archive and rights review findings before we finalize the exhibit plan. The rights check I completed permits each public exhibit audio excerpt to be no longer than exactly 3 minutes, and it requires contributor attribution beside every excerpt. These limits have not yet been added to the exhibit template, so the draft needs to be updated before Dr. Chen signs off.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share findings from my family outreach review. Family outreach confirmed that consent materials must be available in exactly English, Spanish, and Arabic, and that paper consent forms must be offered in addition to the online form. I completed the outreach review, but the family-materials checklist has not yet been revised to reflect these requirements, so the draft needs to be updated before Dr. Chen signs off.
transcript.speaker: A5
